title: The boy behind every vanilla pod
whisper: one flower, one day, one thumb
renderedWith: raea/sillage-004-vanilla (map fields unused; this file holds the script and the voice)

beats.say: In {1841|eighteen forty-one}, a {12|twelve}-year-old boy found a trick. Almost every vanilla pod on Earth still depends on it.
Vanilla is an orchid from Mexico. The bean is its seed pod, picked green.
Planters took the vine to tropical islands. It bloomed. But it gave almost no pods.
In Mexico, a wild bee does the job. Scientists still argue about which one.
And each flower opens for a single day. Miss it, and the flower falls.
Réunion, an island in the Indian Ocean. Edmond is twelve, and enslaved on a plantation.
With a thin stick, he lifts a tiny flap inside the flower. Then his thumb presses the two parts together.
It works. The trick spreads across the island, then the world.
Today, nearly all vanilla is still pollinated like this. By hand.
And Edmond? He is free in {1848|eighteen forty-eight}. He takes the name Albius, from the Latin for white.
He never gets rich from it. He dies poor, in {1880|eighteen eighty}.
Vanilla is now the second most expensive spice, after saffron.
But every real pod still starts with his thumb.
